Liam — thanks for the clear note and the invoice. TL;DR: both workflows are acceptable, we prefer gross where possible but can accept net with reconciliation details. Details below.

Option A — Gross wire (preferred when possible):
- ACME sends the full invoice EUR amount and elects OUR (sender pays all correspondent/intermediary fees).
- Wire fields: include beneficiary name "Redwood Inference Ltd", account IBAN, SWIFT, and reference REDWOOD-12345. Attach your bank's response showing OUR chosen.
- VAT: we'll invoice EUR to the entity you specify; if you provide an EU VAT ID and the payer is a company in the EU, we can apply B2B reverse charge. Otherwise we treat per invoiced entity and local VAT rules apply.

Option B — Net wire (if you must):
- ACME sends net amount (amount credited to our account after intermediary fees). Please include in the wire description the gross invoice amount and the intermediary fee amount in a standard format: "INV:REDWOOD-12345|GROSS:XXXX.XX EUR|INTFEE:YY.YY EUR" so our AR can auto-reconcile.
- We will accept net for this customer as a one-off, but finance needs a reconciliation line item. If intermediary fees exceed a threshold (we typically absorb fees <= 20 EUR), finance will chargeback or issue a one-time credit depending on bucket.

Action items for you: please send the confirmation from your bank with route (corr bank, SWIFT, IBAN) and whether they will mark the wire as OUR/BEN/shared. I've attached a wiring template to show the exact field we need.

Attachments: wire_routing_template.xlsx, Invoice_2026-08-31-REDWOOD-12345.pdf

Related: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/companies/ACME (DEAL-8271)

To confirm VAT treatment we need the billing entity legal name and VAT ID. If you want us to treat this as UK-to-EU routing with FX at the bank, confirm that explicitly. Our treasury prefers not to perform FX on incoming wires; we usually allow the sending bank to convert unless otherwise instructed.

Laura — looping you in for final GL/credit policy on intermediary fee absorption.
